(a) In General.—Subsection (f) of section 45P is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to payments made after December 31, 2011.

fable.w: This section only extends an expiration date in a tax code provision and sets the effective date for payments. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: Subsection (f) of section 45P is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.

opus.w: This section only moves a tax provision's expiration date and sets an effective date. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, required rulemaking, or right to sue. Nothing in it could reasonably be read as participation.
opus.s: Subsection (f) of section 45P is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting but wrong reading:** none really. The section only changes a date in a tax credit (section 45P) and sets when the change takes effect. No one outside the federal government is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue, and no rulemaking is required.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends the expiration date of a tax provision and specifies its effective date. It does not create any advisory committees, public comment periods, consultations with states or tribes, or other mechanisms for outside parties to participate in federal decision-making. The actors involved are limited to the legislative amendment process and the application of the law, which does not constitute participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) In General.—Subsection (f) of section 45P is amended by striking “December 31, 2011” and inserting “December 31, 2013”. 
    (b) Effective Date.—The amendment made by this section shall apply to payments made after December 31, 2011.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the effective date of a tax credit could affect public participation in some indirect way, or that the amendment process itself involves participation. However, the text is purely a technical amendment to a statute's dates and does not establish any process for consulting with or coordinating with outside parties.
